text:
Maya Chen: FYI — seeing a big drop in embeddings throughput for /v1/embeddings (model:redwood-embed-1.0). Started ~2026-02-22 02:13 UTC. Several customers report vectors/sec falling from ~110k -> ~18k, while per-request latency spiked.

Alex Rivera: can you paste a request id and sample payload? any 400s? dimension mismatch errors?

Maya Chen: one repro includes a 400: "embedding dim mismatch: expected 1024, got 1536" for customer A (they changed model family client-side). But the bulk of reports are plain slow responses (200s). Example request_id: req_20260222_2a7b. payload: {"input": ["sentence..."], "model": "redwood-embed-1.0"}

Priya Shah: looking at infra metrics — GPUs show low SM utilization (~22%) but very high memory alloc (~88-92%) on p4d. nginx queue depth per-worker jumped to 12-18. sounds like tiny micro-batches stuffing memory and stalling kernels.

Ben Ortiz: @Priya can you dump nvidia-smi and runtime logs for the node? also what changed in last deploy (eng-runtime)?

infra-bot: deploy redwood/serving-runtime@v2.14.3 rolled at 01:58 UTC by @jen

Priya Shah: pasted nvidia-smi snippet:
```
GPU  Util  Mem%  Temp
0    22%   90%   71C
1    18%   91%   72C
```
also runtime logs:
```
[2026-02-22T02:05:03Z] batcher: max_batch=64, batch_timeout_ms=16
[2026-02-22T02:05:03Z] batcher: avg_batch_size=1.6, inflight_queues=14
[2026-02-22T02:05:04Z] runtime: kernel_launch_time increased x3
```

Alex Rivera: avg_batch_size 1.6 — that explains vectors/sec tank: we have many small batches => kernel overhead dominates. Do we have an A/B rollout for batching heuristics in v2.14.3?

Maya Chen: customers are hitting 20-30 RPS per instance but each request small (1-2 inputs). Previously continuous batching grouped them to 32ish.

Priya Shah: checking commit diff — v2.14.3 PR reverted a change that added adaptive batching warmup; also changed default batch_timeout_ms from 64 -> 16 to reduce p99 latency for large requests. That makes small-batch workloads worse.

Ben Ortiz: can we flip flag to old defaults in prod? Is config dynamic?

Priya Shah: batcher has runtime flag `--batch-timeout-ms`. it's in configmap; patching now to set 64.

Alex Rivera: also we should confirm KV cache/prefix caching behavior — if cache disabled, more mem usage and smaller effective batches. Any change to kv-cache in that deploy?

Priya Shah: no kv config changes in deploy. kernel telemetry suggests many small kernels starting/stopping.

Maya Chen: repro steps for SRE to validate locally:
1) run loadgen: `./loadgen --endpoint /v1/embeddings --model redwood-embed-1.0 --concurrency 12 --batch-size 1 --qps 30 --payload-size 1`
2) compare avg_batch_size and vectors/sec

Ben Ortiz: doing the config patch now. Rolling patch to set batch-timeout back to 64ms on canary 2 nodes.

deploy-bot: rollout started redwood/serving-runtime@v2.14.3-canary-patch (2 nodes)

Priya Shah: canary metrics look good — avg_batch_size ~28, vectors/sec back up ~105k across the two nodes. GPU util increased to 68%.

Maya Chen: customer replies: latency and throughput restored. no additional 400s. thumbs up from them :thumbsup: 

Alex Rivera: root cause: perf regression introduced by reducing batch timeout to 16ms to help large requests; negative impact on small-doc embeddings. Action: add workload-specific batching profile and telemetry alert for avg_batch_size < 8.

Maya Chen: filing followup ticket with customers and docs. PR for config change: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/3812

Ben Ortiz: closing thread once patch fully rolled. thanks all.

Priya Shah: note for postmortem: consider auto-profiles by endpoint + model vector size.

Maya Chen: resolved for now — will update if anything else pops up.
